It is NOT the work of /claude/a0_atlas, which this file names as agent_run_id because the protocol allows one author handoff per work package and a ratchet binds that field to the manifest's author_agent_run_id. Batches 011, 020, 021, 030 and 040 said the same thing about their own authors, for the same reason.

THE SHAPE THE BATCH TURNS ON, stated first because everything else follows from it: batch 050 creates three TENANT tables and writes NO POLICY AND NO CLIENT GRANT. §8.4 gives this family two rows and neither is implementable by a migration. "Job redacted status SELECT | Y | Y | O/P | O/P | O/P | P" grants a REDACTED STATUS, whose object is a security_invoker view on a read allowlist RFC-2026-012 §3 and RFC-2026-021 §7 keep empty. "Internal job/attempt/DLQ payload | N N N N N S" is the schema's FIRST `S` cell, whose shape RFC-2026-016 §2 describes with a workspace GUC no document names, for a role RFC-2026-019 §4/3 says nothing can yet be, in a form that cannot express a queue's own claim query. The outbox and the consumer ledger have no §8 row at all. So all three tables are ENABLE + FORCE with an empty policy set, which is batch 030's state on GLOBAL tables arriving for the first time on TENANT ones.

THE COLUMNS ARE TWO CONTRACTS' PROPERTIES RATHER THAN A DESIGN, which inverts the discipline every earlier batch had to apply. 010, 020, 030 and 040 each recorded that §5 names no column of their family and invented none. CTR-JOB-001 and CTR-EVT-001 name every field, with types, bounds and patterns -- so app.jobs carries exactly CTR-JOB-001's properties minus tenant_context (resolved to §3.3's canonical workspace_id), app.outbox_events carries exactly CTR-EVT-001's minus tenant_context and minus `payload` (fixed at maxProperties 0 by the contract itself), and a static test reads both schema files and requires a column per property. Every pattern is the contract's own string, character for character, non-capturing groups included.

A JOB ROW IS TENANT-SCOPED, AND THREE DOCUMENTS AGREE WITHOUT ARGUMENT: §5 scopes jobs.kernel to `workspace`, §4's ERD reads WORKSPACE ||--o{ JOB : queues, and CTR-JOB-001 requires a tenant_context whose workspace_id CTR-TEN-001 makes mandatory. All three tables carry `workspace_id uuid not null references app.workspaces (id)`. Nothing BELOW the tenant is carried: CTR-TEN-001 makes business_profile_id and page_context_profile_id optional, and §5 plus §4 give this family no scope below the workspace, so an event about a Business records it in CTR-EVT-001's own `subject` instead (030's sentence about a page-level assignment, one family over).

NO created_by AND NO updated_by ON ANY OF THE THREE. §3.2 adds the audit actor columns for a USER MUTATION, and §8 grants no client any write on any table in this family, so they would be two nullable uuids nothing writes -- 030's reading on the global catalog, applied to a tenant table for the first time. CTR-TEN-001's `actor` is not stored either, and the contract's own trust boundary is why: the tenant context is "Server-resolved only after membership and Workspace->Business->Page relation validation", so a context frozen onto a row and replayed at claim time is an earlier request's resolution being re-trusted.

security_privacy_cost_impact:
This increment creates the first INTERNAL-3 rows in the schema, and its security answer is a refusal rather than a boundary.

WHAT IT EXPOSES: NOTHING. No client role -- `authenticated` or `anon` -- is granted any privilege on app.jobs, app.outbox_events or app.consumer_ledger, and no policy exists on any of them. §9.1 classes INTERNAL-3 "private; short retention" with the client projection "redacted status only", and §8.4's client cell grants exactly that projection -- an object RFC-2026-012 §2/§3 and RFC-2026-021 §7 reserve to an RFC. So the whole family is unreachable from the request path, and the isolation suite asserts that from every client identity, at the layer each refusal actually lands on: the TABLE for `authenticated`, which holds USAGE on schema app, and the SCHEMA for `anon`, which holds nothing anywhere.

WHAT IT REFUSES TO EXPOSE, AND WHY THAT IS THE SECURITY WORK. A client that could write an outbox row would choose the event_type, the producer and the subject every consumer downstream routes and trusts on: a forged domain event is not a leaked row, it is an instruction. §3.4 nevertheless requires the outbox row to be written in the SAME TRANSACTION as the domain state, and the only thing that writes domain state today is a client -- so the rule is unsatisfiable and is recorded as owed to the command surface rather than paid with a client grant or a trigger.

WHAT REACHES A WORKER, IN A REFERENCE AND NEVER IN CONTENT. §3.4 forbids a secret, a binary, a long-lived signed URL or a raw provider response in a job payload, and §9.2 repeats it. app.jobs therefore carries `input_ref` and `result_ref` and no payload column, each constrained by CTR-JOB-001's own reference pattern -- whose x-reference-rule records that the earlier deny-list form passed `HTTPS://host/x`, `//host/x`, `file:///etc/passwd`, `javascript:` and `../../../etc/passwd`. A worker dereferences these values, so the constraint is on the column and not only on the wire. app.outbox_events carries no payload column at all, because CTR-EVT-001 fixes `payload` at maxProperties 0 until a domain payload contract is owner-approved.

THE ONE PRIVILEGE THIS BATCH DOES GRANT is app_worker's, and it exists to make a denial falsifiable rather than to enable anything: with the grant and no policy, an empty read can only have come from row level security, and a service role that had quietly acquired BYPASSRLS would SUCCEED where the suite demands a refusal. On these three tables that is the whole of the live evidence.

COST: none beyond storage. No external provider, no secret, no network, no new role, no new schema, and no grant to app_command or app_maintenance.
migration_and_data_impact:
One new forward migration, db/foundation/migrations/050_async_kernel.sql, creating three tables, five indexes, two updated_at triggers, ZERO policies and an apply-time assertion block. It rewrites no merged migration: it contains no `drop policy` and no `alter table` naming a table another batch owns, and a static test asserts both rather than trusting the header.

IT IS DECLARED NOT APPLIED TO THE PROVISIONED INSTANCE, extending the tail 011, 020, 021, 030 and 040 already form -- and for a DIFFERENT reason from any of them. Its three tables reference app.workspaces and nothing else, so every SQL dependency it has is already there: 050 is the first batch in that tail that COULD be applied. The declaration must name a TAIL of the ordered set, because a database holding 050 while missing five predecessors is DIVERGENT rather than behind, and this run may issue no DDL to the instance in any case. The migration set is now TWELVE files; CI applies all twelve to a postgres:17 container on every pull request.

TWO NEW SHAPES THE SCHEMA HAS NOT HELD BEFORE. §3.2's second identifier rule -- "Append-only event/attempt/ledger ปริมาณสูง: bigint generated always as identity" -- lands for the first time, on app.outbox_events and app.consumer_ledger. ALWAYS and not BY DEFAULT, asserted from pg_attribute.attidentity, because under BY DEFAULT a writer may choose its own position in an ordered log and the outbox's id IS the relay's cursor. And app.outbox_events carries BOTH a bigint `id` and a uuid `event_id`, which is not two sources of truth for one fact: the bigint orders and the uuid identifies, and app.consumer_ledger records the second.

NO DATA MIGRATION AND NO BACKFILL. The tables are empty on creation; the only rows anywhere are the six the isolation fixture loads administratively in CI.

known_limitations:
BATCH 050 MET RFC-2026-016 §2's AMENDMENT ON THE FIRST TABLE IT WOULD LAND ON, AND THE SHAPE DOES NOT FIT. That decision (approved 2026-09-05) amends §8.5 so that a policy is "`TO authenticated` for user paths and `TO <service role>` for each operation the matrix already marks `S`, with the service policy scoped by a server-set workspace GUC derived from the server-resolved tenant context CTR-TEN-001 already requires". §8.4's "Internal job/attempt/DLQ payload | N N N N N S" is the FIRST `S` CELL ANY BATCH IN THIS SCHEMA HAS OWNED -- batch 010's header predicted this batch by name -- and 050 writes no service policy. Three reasons, and the third is a finding about the decision rather than about this batch.

(1) NO DOCUMENT NAMES THE GUC. RFC-2026-016 §2 says "a server-set workspace GUC" and spells none. Batch 011 could inline the platform's identity expression because it MEASURED `request.jwt.claims` off the provisioned instance and pinned the literal in scripts/db/run.mjs; there is no equivalent measurement here, because nothing on any instance sets a workspace GUC. Writing `current_setting('app.workspace_id', true)` would fix that name for 051, 061, 070, 100, 110, 120, 131 and 140.

(2) NOTHING CAN BE app_worker. RFC-2026-019 §4/3, approved 2026-09-06 and NEWER than RFC-2026-016: "app_worker's connection method is not decided here, and saying so is the decision. No background worker exists."

(3) THE AMENDMENT'S SHAPE CANNOT EXPRESS A QUEUE'S CLAIM QUERY, WHICH IS NEW AND IS THE PART A0 AND A1 OWE AN ANSWER TO. §3.4 specifies how a worker takes work: "Worker claim ใช้ lease + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED หรือ queue semantics ที่เทียบเท่า". A claim query asks for the next due job and CANNOT NAME A WORKSPACE, because which workspace the next job belongs to is what reading the row tells you. A policy scoped by one workspace GUC therefore refuses every claim, or forces a worker to poll workspace by workspace, which is not a queue. RFC-2026-016 §2 is not wrong -- it was written about the other `S` cells (research rows, publish delivery, notification state, usage ledger, audit inserts), where the worker is acting on a KNOWN row and already holds the tenant context. A JOB QUEUE is the one family in §8's four matrices where the service DISCOVERS the context by reading the row. Disposing of this belongs to RFC-2026-016's owner (A0) with A1 Security, not to a batch routing around it.

§3.4's ONE RULE ABOUT THE OUTBOX CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY ANY WRITE PATH THIS SCHEMA HAS, and batch 050 records it rather than working around it. §3.4's first bullet is "Domain state และ outbox event เขียน transaction เดียวกัน" -- the domain state and its outbox event are written in the SAME TRANSACTION. Follow it through: domain state is written by `authenticated` directly (020, 030 and 040 each record that no command function exists for their module; RFC-2026-019 §2 measured zero functions owned by app_command on the instance), so "the same transaction" is today a CLIENT's -- and a client that could write an outbox row would choose `event_type`, `producer.module_key`, `producer.implementation_version` and `subject`, which are the four fields every consumer downstream routes and trusts on. A forged `content.version.approved` is not a leaked row; it is an instruction to the rest of the system.

So `authenticated` is granted NOTHING on app.outbox_events -- §8 has no cell for an outbox row anywhere and §9.1 classes the family INTERNAL-3 -- and the table is correctly shaped with NO WRITER. A TRIGGER IS REFUSED TWICE OVER and the refusal is worth recording because it is the obvious workaround: migration invariant 1 forbids 050 touching a merged migration, and §3.4's own last bullet forbids a module writing another module's table directly. Batch 040 refused to invent a trigger for the adjacent gap (§15); this refusal has that reason plus one more. Owed to the command surface, which RFC-2026-012 §4 names and DATA-DEC-03 owns.

THE JOB REDACTED-STATUS VIEW IS THE STRONGEST READ-ALLOWLIST CANDIDATE THIS REPOSITORY HAS AND BATCH 050 MAY NOT ADD IT. §8.4's "Job redacted status SELECT" is `Y` for owner and admin -- a REAL client cell, unlike the industry catalog, which RFC-2026-021 §5 disposed of with no §8 row at all. The object that cell grants is a REDACTED STATUS: §9.1 gives INTERNAL-3 the client projection "redacted status only", and the next row of §8.4 marks the internal job payload `N` for every client role, so a base-table grant would hand a client both rows of one matrix at once. A projection object is a security_invoker view, and RFC-2026-012 §2/§3 plus RFC-2026-021 §7 put every such view on an allowlist that is EMPTY and grows only by RFC.

AGAINST RFC-2026-021 §4's CRITERIA, checked rather than cited: C1 FAILS TODAY -- there is no `src/`, no client module and no screen named in any source document that reads a job's status. C7 DOES NOT APPLY, and this is where the candidate is stronger than the catalog: app.jobs is a TENANT table, so the policy behind the view is `app.is_active_member(workspace_id)`, a predicate RLS can express, and a mistake reaches one workspace. C2/C3 are the work: "redacted status" has to be enumerated, and 050's header proposes the column list (id, workspace_id, job_type, available_at, attempt, max_attempts, progress_percent, progress_stage, cancel_requested_at, created_at, updated_at) with input_ref, result_ref, lease_owner, lease_expires_at and last_error_code EXCLUDED, so a reviewer can disagree before it is a grant. C6 raises a question no document answers: §8.4 marks editor, approver and viewer `O/P` -- BOTH SYMBOLS IN ONE CELL -- and `O` on a job would mean "the job I started", which needs an actor column this family does not have.

AND THE DEBT THIS BATCH DOES NOT ADD TO: RFC-2026-021 §8.5 requires the known-exceptions list of inherited `authenticated` base-table grants to be CLOSED, and 030 and 040 grew it from three batches to five while the list still does not exist. BATCH 050 ADDS NO `authenticated` GRANT ANYWHERE, so it is the first batch since that list was described to leave it at five rather than six.

CTR-JOB-001 BOUNDS TWO REFERENCE-SHAPED FIELDS AND LEAVES FOUR UNBOUNDED, REPORTED TO ITS OWNER (A0) RATHER THAN FIXED BY A MIGRATION. `job_id` and `dedupe_key` carry maxLength 128 and `input_ref`/`result_ref` carry 256, each with an x-bound-note recording that independent security review found reference-shaped fields on these envelopes with no pattern AND no bound, "so each accepted a 100000-character value". Four fields beside them have `minLength: 1` and NO maximum: `job_type`, `lease_owner`, `progress_stage` and `last_error_code`. CTR-EVT-001 bounded every one of its equivalents in RFC-2026-009; CTR-JOB-001 did not.

Batch 050 adds no invented maximum. A CHECK stricter than the wire would reject an envelope the contract accepts, and a migration may not amend a contract -- which is the same treatment 030 gave the undefined CATALOG retention class. A static test asserts that all four are STILL unbounded, so the day the contract's owner bounds one, this batch's constraints are asked to gain the bound in the same change instead of drifting apart quietly.

§5 ASSIGNS jobs.kernel THE RETENTION CLASSES `JOB-SHORT/LEDGER` AND §10 DEFINES NO CLASS CALLED `LEDGER`. Its table has twenty-six rows and none of them is that one. This is the SECOND time a family has named a class the retention baseline does not define -- batch 030 reported the same about `CATALOG` for industry.core -- so it is a finding about §10 rather than about either batch, and it is owned by A1 Data and by §10's own Product/Security/Legal approval (§15). The three classes that ARE defined are the ones these tables belong to: JOB-SHORT ("30 วัน success; 90 วัน failed/DLQ"), OUTBOX-SHORT ("จน consumers ack + 30 วัน") and CONSUMER-LEDGER ("180 วันหรือ max replay window"). None of their numbers is written into a constraint, a default or an index predicate: batch 160 owns the job and §10's approval owns the numbers. What 050 does provide is the column each sweep would read and an index over it, which is 010's treatment of `expires_at` for TOKEN-SHORT before that job existed either.

THE SAME TWO CLASSES ALSO DECIDE A CONSTRAINT, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECISION. app.consumer_ledger has NO foreign key to app.outbox_events: OUTBOX-SHORT purges an event at ack + 30 days while CONSUMER-LEDGER keeps a ledger row for 180 days or the max replay window, so the key would take the ledger row with the event and destroy the replay safety the longer window exists for. The ledger records that an event id WAS consumed; it does not record a row.

A CITATION CORRECTION, RECORDED RATHER THAN PROPAGATED. The dispatch for this batch cites "§12.6 assertion 9" for "Retry idempotent ไม่สร้าง package ที่เข้าถึงข้าม scope". §12.6 -- the deterministic fixture contract -- has EIGHT required smoke assertions and no ninth; that sentence is item 9 of §11.1, the PDPA/data-export contract. The PRINCIPLE is general and batch 050 applies it: it is why `workspace_id` is in app.consumer_ledger's natural key, alongside CTR-IDM-001's own rule that an idempotency key's scope includes the workspace. The POSITION was not, and SMOKE_COVERAGE therefore gains no ninth key -- batch 030 refused to invent one for a shape §12.6 has no row for and this batch keeps that rule. A positional citation into a numbered list is the defect D11 recorded in the evidence layer; this is the third time it has been met.

BATCH 050 CREATES THREE TABLES AND REFUSES TWO THAT THREE DOCUMENTS NAME, and the two refusals have different reasons. §5's inventory reads "jobs/attempts/DLQ/outbox/consumed ledger", §6's registry describes 050 as "jobs/outbox/consumer ledger", and §4's ERD contains WORKSPACE ||--o{ JOB and JOB ||--o{ JOB_ATTEMPT. Five names, three names, two entities.

NO app.job_attempts. The ERD does carry JOB_ATTEMPT, so "the registry does not name it" would be a thin reason alone. The deciding one is that CTR-JOB-001 models attempts as SCALARS ON THE ENVELOPE -- `attempt`, `max_attempts` and `last_error_code` -- so those columns exist because the contract requires them, and an attempt TABLE beside them would be a second source of truth for "how many attempts" that nothing in this schema could keep equal: no command function binds "insert an attempt row" and "increment job.attempt" into one transaction. That is 021's reason for refusing current_version_id, 030's for refusing industry_pack_id and 040's for refusing a kind column on a version, a fourth time. If a later decision wants attempt ROWS -- §10's JOB-SHORT does say "attempt errors" -- the honest form is a batch that adds the table AND makes `attempt` derived, which is a change to CTR-JOB-001's envelope and therefore A0's act on the contract.

NO DEAD-LETTER TABLE, AND NO STATUS COLUMN ANYWHERE. A DLQ is a STATE, and CTR-JOB-001's manifest closes who may name states: "Candidate only; lifecycle state names and transition policy remain subject to source-defined owner review." The envelope has NO status field. So the lifecycle is the timestamps and counters the contract names -- available_at, lease_owner/lease_expires_at, attempt/max_attempts, cancel_requested_at (§11.4 step 3's "cancel or drain jobs using typed policy"), result_ref, last_error_code -- and "dead-lettered" is a QUERY. §3.2's "Phase 1 state: text + named CHECK" is a rule about HOW a state is stored once somebody with the authority has decided what the states ARE.

THE SAME REFUSAL LANDS IN AN INDEX, which is where it is quietest. The obvious claim index is `(available_at) where result_ref is null and cancel_requested_at is null and attempt < max_attempts` -- and that predicate IS a definition of which jobs are still live. The index is over available_at alone. An index predicate is not a weaker place to put a decision than a CHECK constraint; it is a quieter one.

THREE OUTCOME KINDS ARE STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE ON BATCH 050's TABLES, and the suite says so instead of faking them. Because no client role holds a grant and no policy exists: (1) NO `rows` CASE IS POSSIBLE -- no identity can read any of the three tables, so there is no positive to pair a negative against, and what stands in its place is the SERVICE's filtered read. (2) NO `no-effect` CASE IS POSSIBLE -- that kind is an empty result PLUS a witness read by an identity that can see the target row, and there is no such identity for any row, so a filtered UPDATE cannot be asserted at all and the write path is carried by the INSERT, which raises. (3) NO `rejected` CASE IS POSSIBLE -- a duplicate ledger insert never reaches the unique constraint, because app_worker holds the INSERT grant, finds no permissive policy and is refused with 42501 first, so a case demanding 23505 would assert an outcome a correct database cannot produce. Batch 040 met that last shape on its forged-scope inserts and recorded it rather than faking a case; the ledger's natural key is asserted instead by 050's apply-time block, which reads it out of pg_constraint as a sorted COLUMN SET.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE COVERAGE MAP, stated rather than absorbed: §12.6/1 and §8.6/5 are NOT claimed on this family. These are the first TENANT tables in the schema whose boundary cannot be observed -- both owners are refused identically at the privilege layer, exactly as on batch 030's GLOBAL rows and for a completely different reason -- and counting that as isolation would report a refusal that holds for everybody as a boundary that holds for one tenant. §12.6/5 is not claimed either: its three cases carry `§12.6/5-analogue`, because a suspended member refused where every active member is also refused has been refused by the privilege system and not by suspension. §12.6/6 and §12.6/8 are extended honestly and no row moves.

BATCH 050 IS DECLARED NOT APPLIED TO THE PROVISIONED INSTANCE, extending the tail 011, 020, 021, 030 and 040 already form -- AND FOR A DIFFERENT REASON FROM ANY OF THEM. Its three tables reference app.workspaces and nothing else, so every SQL dependency it has IS on that instance: it is the first batch in the tail that COULD be applied. It is declared not applied because the declaration must name a TAIL of the ordered set, which scripts/db/run.mjs enforces -- a database holding 050 while missing five of its predecessors is DIVERGENT rather than behind, a different finding with a different fix -- and because this run may issue no DDL to the instance. THE MIGRATION SET IS NOW TWELVE FILES: 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010, 011, 020, 021, 030, 040 and 050, counted from the tree. CI applies all twelve to a postgres:17 container on every pull request; this development host has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so every live claim in batch 050 -- the apply-time block, the 239 isolation cases and three negative-control entries -- is proven by a CI round and by nothing else.

(3) THE AMENDMENT'S SHAPE CANNOT EXPRESS A QUEUE'S CLAIM QUERY, WHICH IS NEW AND IS THE PART A0 AND A1 OWE AN ANSWER TO. §3.4 specifies how a worker takes work: "Worker claim ใช้ lease + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED หรือ queue semantics ที่เทียบเท่า". A claim query asks for the next due job and CANNOT NAME A WORKSPACE, because which workspace the next job belongs to is what reading the row tells you. A policy scoped by one workspace GUC therefore refuses every claim, or forces a worker to poll workspace by workspace, which is not a queue. RFC-2026-016 §2 is not wrong -- it was written about the other `S` cells (research rows, publish delivery, notification state, usage ledger, audit inserts), where the worker is acting on a KNOWN row and already holds the tenant context. A JOB QUEUE is the one family in §8's four matrices where the service DISCOVERS the context by reading the row. Disposing of this belongs to RFC-2026-016's owner (A0) with A1 Security, not to a batch routing around it.

§3.4's ONE RULE ABOUT THE OUTBOX CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY ANY WRITE PATH THIS SCHEMA HAS, and batch 050 records it rather than working around it. §3.4's first bullet is "Domain state และ outbox event เขียน transaction เดียวกัน" -- the domain state and its outbox event are written in the SAME TRANSACTION. Follow it through: domain state is written by `authenticated` directly (020, 030 and 040 each record that no command function exists for their module; RFC-2026-019 §2 measured zero functions owned by app_command on the instance), so "the same transaction" is today a CLIENT's -- and a client that could write an outbox row would choose `event_type`, `producer.module_key`, `producer.implementation_version` and `subject`, which are the four fields every consumer downstream routes and trusts on. A forged `content.version.approved` is not a leaked row; it is an instruction to the rest of the system.

So `authenticated` is granted NOTHING on app.outbox_events -- §8 has no cell for an outbox row anywhere and §9.1 classes the family INTERNAL-3 -- and the table is correctly shaped with NO WRITER. A TRIGGER IS REFUSED TWICE OVER and the refusal is worth recording because it is the obvious workaround: migration invariant 1 forbids 050 touching a merged migration, and §3.4's own last bullet forbids a module writing another module's table directly. Batch 040 refused to invent a trigger for the adjacent gap (§15); this refusal has that reason plus one more. Owed to the command surface, which RFC-2026-012 §4 names and DATA-DEC-03 owns.

THE JOB REDACTED-STATUS VIEW IS THE STRONGEST READ-ALLOWLIST CANDIDATE THIS REPOSITORY HAS AND BATCH 050 MAY NOT ADD IT. §8.4's "Job redacted status SELECT" is `Y` for owner and admin -- a REAL client cell, unlike the industry catalog, which RFC-2026-021 §5 disposed of with no §8 row at all. The object that cell grants is a REDACTED STATUS: §9.1 gives INTERNAL-3 the client projection "redacted status only", and the next row of §8.4 marks the internal job payload `N` for every client role, so a base-table grant would hand a client both rows of one matrix at once. A projection object is a security_invoker view, and RFC-2026-012 §2/§3 plus RFC-2026-021 §7 put every such view on an allowlist that is EMPTY and grows only by RFC.

AGAINST RFC-2026-021 §4's CRITERIA, checked rather than cited: C1 FAILS TODAY -- there is no `src/`, no client module and no screen named in any source document that reads a job's status. C7 DOES NOT APPLY, and this is where the candidate is stronger than the catalog: app.jobs is a TENANT table, so the policy behind the view is `app.is_active_member(workspace_id)`, a predicate RLS can express, and a mistake reaches one workspace. C2/C3 are the work: "redacted status" has to be enumerated, and 050's header proposes the column list (id, workspace_id, job_type, available_at, attempt, max_attempts, progress_percent, progress_stage, cancel_requested_at, created_at, updated_at) with input_ref, result_ref, lease_owner, lease_expires_at and last_error_code EXCLUDED, so a reviewer can disagree before it is a grant. C6 raises a question no document answers: §8.4 marks editor, approver and viewer `O/P` -- BOTH SYMBOLS IN ONE CELL -- and `O` on a job would mean "the job I started", which needs an actor column this family does not have.

AND THE DEBT THIS BATCH DOES NOT ADD TO: RFC-2026-021 §8.5 requires the known-exceptions list of inherited `authenticated` base-table grants to be CLOSED, and 030 and 040 grew it from three batches to five while the list still does not exist. BATCH 050 ADDS NO `authenticated` GRANT ANYWHERE, so it is the first batch since that list was described to leave it at five rather than six.

CTR-JOB-001 BOUNDS TWO REFERENCE-SHAPED FIELDS AND LEAVES FOUR UNBOUNDED, REPORTED TO ITS OWNER (A0) RATHER THAN FIXED BY A MIGRATION. `job_id` and `dedupe_key` carry maxLength 128 and `input_ref`/`result_ref` carry 256, each with an x-bound-note recording that independent security review found reference-shaped fields on these envelopes with no pattern AND no bound, "so each accepted a 100000-character value". Four fields beside them have `minLength: 1` and NO maximum: `job_type`, `lease_owner`, `progress_stage` and `last_error_code`. CTR-EVT-001 bounded every one of its equivalents in RFC-2026-009; CTR-JOB-001 did not.

Batch 050 adds no invented maximum. A CHECK stricter than the wire would reject an envelope the contract accepts, and a migration may not amend a contract -- which is the same treatment 030 gave the undefined CATALOG retention class. A static test asserts that all four are STILL unbounded, so the day the contract's owner bounds one, this batch's constraints are asked to gain the bound in the same change instead of drifting apart quietly.

§5 ASSIGNS jobs.kernel THE RETENTION CLASSES `JOB-SHORT/LEDGER` AND §10 DEFINES NO CLASS CALLED `LEDGER`. Its table has twenty-six rows and none of them is that one. This is the SECOND time a family has named a class the retention baseline does not define -- batch 030 reported the same about `CATALOG` for industry.core -- so it is a finding about §10 rather than about either batch, and it is owned by A1 Data and by §10's own Product/Security/Legal approval (§15). The three classes that ARE defined are the ones these tables belong to: JOB-SHORT ("30 วัน success; 90 วัน failed/DLQ"), OUTBOX-SHORT ("จน consumers ack + 30 วัน") and CONSUMER-LEDGER ("180 วันหรือ max replay window"). None of their numbers is written into a constraint, a default or an index predicate: batch 160 owns the job and §10's approval owns the numbers. What 050 does provide is the column each sweep would read and an index over it, which is 010's treatment of `expires_at` for TOKEN-SHORT before that job existed either.

THE SAME TWO CLASSES ALSO DECIDE A CONSTRAINT, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECISION. app.consumer_ledger has NO foreign key to app.outbox_events: OUTBOX-SHORT purges an event at ack + 30 days while CONSUMER-LEDGER keeps a ledger row for 180 days or the max replay window, so the key would take the ledger row with the event and destroy the replay safety the longer window exists for. The ledger records that an event id WAS consumed; it does not record a row.

A CITATION CORRECTION, RECORDED RATHER THAN PROPAGATED. The dispatch for this batch cites "§12.6 assertion 9" for "Retry idempotent ไม่สร้าง package ที่เข้าถึงข้าม scope". §12.6 -- the deterministic fixture contract -- has EIGHT required smoke assertions and no ninth; that sentence is item 9 of §11.1, the PDPA/data-export contract. The PRINCIPLE is general and batch 050 applies it: it is why `workspace_id` is in app.consumer_ledger's natural key, alongside CTR-IDM-001's own rule that an idempotency key's scope includes the workspace. The POSITION was not, and SMOKE_COVERAGE therefore gains no ninth key -- batch 030 refused to invent one for a shape §12.6 has no row for and this batch keeps that rule. A positional citation into a numbered list is the defect D11 recorded in the evidence layer; this is the third time it has been met.

BATCH 050 CREATES THREE TABLES AND REFUSES TWO THAT THREE DOCUMENTS NAME, and the two refusals have different reasons. §5's inventory reads "jobs/attempts/DLQ/outbox/consumed ledger", §6's registry describes 050 as "jobs/outbox/consumer ledger", and §4's ERD contains WORKSPACE ||--o{ JOB and JOB ||--o{ JOB_ATTEMPT. Five names, three names, two entities.

NO app.job_attempts. The ERD does carry JOB_ATTEMPT, so "the registry does not name it" would be a thin reason alone. The deciding one is that CTR-JOB-001 models attempts as SCALARS ON THE ENVELOPE -- `attempt`, `max_attempts` and `last_error_code` -- so those columns exist because the contract requires them, and an attempt TABLE beside them would be a second source of truth for "how many attempts" that nothing in this schema could keep equal: no command function binds "insert an attempt row" and "increment job.attempt" into one transaction. That is 021's reason for refusing current_version_id, 030's for refusing industry_pack_id and 040's for refusing a kind column on a version, a fourth time. If a later decision wants attempt ROWS -- §10's JOB-SHORT does say "attempt errors" -- the honest form is a batch that adds the table AND makes `attempt` derived, which is a change to CTR-JOB-001's envelope and therefore A0's act on the contract.

NO DEAD-LETTER TABLE, AND NO STATUS COLUMN ANYWHERE. A DLQ is a STATE, and CTR-JOB-001's manifest closes who may name states: "Candidate only; lifecycle state names and transition policy remain subject to source-defined owner review." The envelope has NO status field. So the lifecycle is the timestamps and counters the contract names -- available_at, lease_owner/lease_expires_at, attempt/max_attempts, cancel_requested_at (§11.4 step 3's "cancel or drain jobs using typed policy"), result_ref, last_error_code -- and "dead-lettered" is a QUERY. §3.2's "Phase 1 state: text + named CHECK" is a rule about HOW a state is stored once somebody with the authority has decided what the states ARE.

THE SAME REFUSAL LANDS IN AN INDEX, which is where it is quietest. The obvious claim index is `(available_at) where result_ref is null and cancel_requested_at is null and attempt < max_attempts` -- and that predicate IS a definition of which jobs are still live. The index is over available_at alone. An index predicate is not a weaker place to put a decision than a CHECK constraint; it is a quieter one.

THREE OUTCOME KINDS ARE STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE ON BATCH 050's TABLES, and the suite says so instead of faking them. Because no client role holds a grant and no policy exists: (1) NO `rows` CASE IS POSSIBLE -- no identity can read any of the three tables, so there is no positive to pair a negative against, and what stands in its place is the SERVICE's filtered read. (2) NO `no-effect` CASE IS POSSIBLE -- that kind is an empty result PLUS a witness read by an identity that can see the target row, and there is no such identity for any row, so a filtered UPDATE cannot be asserted at all and the write path is carried by the INSERT, which raises. (3) NO `rejected` CASE IS POSSIBLE -- a duplicate ledger insert never reaches the unique constraint, because app_worker holds the INSERT grant, finds no permissive policy and is refused with 42501 first, so a case demanding 23505 would assert an outcome a correct database cannot produce. Batch 040 met that last shape on its forged-scope inserts and recorded it rather than faking a case; the ledger's natural key is asserted instead by 050's apply-time block, which reads it out of pg_constraint as a sorted COLUMN SET.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE COVERAGE MAP, stated rather than absorbed: §12.6/1 and §8.6/5 are NOT claimed on this family. These are the first TENANT tables in the schema whose boundary cannot be observed -- both owners are refused identically at the privilege layer, exactly as on batch 030's GLOBAL rows and for a completely different reason -- and counting that as isolation would report a refusal that holds for everybody as a boundary that holds for one tenant. §12.6/5 is not claimed either: its three cases carry `§12.6/5-analogue`, because a suspended member refused where every active member is also refused has been refused by the privilege system and not by suspension. §12.6/6 and §12.6/8 are extended honestly and no row moves.

BATCH 050 IS DECLARED NOT APPLIED TO THE PROVISIONED INSTANCE, extending the tail 011, 020, 021, 030 and 040 already form -- AND FOR A DIFFERENT REASON FROM ANY OF THEM. Its three tables reference app.workspaces and nothing else, so every SQL dependency it has IS on that instance: it is the first batch in the tail that COULD be applied. It is declared not applied because the declaration must name a TAIL of the ordered set, which scripts/db/run.mjs enforces -- a database holding 050 while missing five of its predecessors is DIVERGENT rather than behind, a different finding with a different fix -- and because this run may issue no DDL to the instance. THE MIGRATION SET IS NOW TWELVE FILES: 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010, 011, 020, 021, 030, 040 and 050, counted from the tree. CI applies all twelve to a postgres:17 container on every pull request; this development host has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so every live claim in batch 050 -- the apply-time block, the 239 isolation cases and three negative-control entries -- is proven by a CI round and by nothing else.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. Nothing here is applied to the provisioned instance, so a revert removes three tables that exist only in CI and in the migration set; there is no data to recover and no forward fix to sequence. What a revert also removes is the record of three findings this branch produced by implementing an approved decision -- that RFC-2026-016 §2's service-policy shape cannot express a queue's claim query, that §3.4's outbox atomicity is unsatisfiable without a command surface, and that §5 names a `LEDGER` retention class §10 does not define -- so a revert should carry those three forward into whatever replaces it.
recommended_next_work_packages: A DISPOSITION ON RFC-2026-016 §2's SERVICE-POLICY SHAPE, owned by A0 with A1 Security. It is the largest thing this batch could not do and it blocks the same cell in 051, 061, 070, 120 and 140. Three things need deciding together: the workspace GUC's NAME (measured, not chosen from memory), how a session becomes app_worker (RFC-2026-019 §4/3 left it open on purpose), and what a service policy looks like on a table where the worker DISCOVERS the tenant context by reading the row rather than arriving with it. The third is new and is a queue's problem specifically.

BATCH 051 (notification inbox/preferences/push), which §6 makes depend on 050. It meets §8.4's "Notification insert/delivery state | N N N N N S" -- the second `S` cell -- and it inherits this batch's refusal rather than a pattern. It also has something 050 does not: §8.4 marks "Own notification SELECT/mark read" `O` for every role, which is an own-row client cell a policy CAN express, so 051 is the batch where the client half of §8.4 becomes implementable.

A COMMAND SURFACE, owned by whoever owns app_command's first function. It is now owed by four batches for four different reasons, and 050's is the sharpest: §3.4 REQUIRES the domain state and its outbox event in one transaction, and no write path in this schema can do it. Until then app.outbox_events is a correctly shaped table with no writer, and §8.6 case 10 -- "Authorized server command -> pass + expected audit/outbox" -- stays unpayable with only one half missing.

BATCH 160 (retention), which owns every purge this family needs: JOB-SHORT, OUTBOX-SHORT and CONSUMER-LEDGER. 050 provides the column each sweep reads and an index over it and encodes no number, because §10's own Product/Security/Legal approval owns those. It should also carry, or escalate, the `LEDGER` class §5 names and §10 does not define.

AN RFC FOR THE JOB REDACTED-STATUS VIEW, whenever a client caller exists. It is the strongest allowlist candidate this repository has -- a real §8.4 cell on a TENANT table, so RFC-2026-021's C7 does not apply -- and it fails only C1. 050's header proposes the column list so the RFC starts from a read rather than a blank page.
reviewer_instructions: READ THE THREE REASONS FOR WRITING NO SERVICE POLICY FIRST, and press on the third. The first two are citations -- RFC-2026-016 §2 names no GUC, RFC-2026-019 §4/3 says nothing can be app_worker -- and a reviewer can check them in a minute. The third is an argument this batch makes on its own: §3.4's lease claim (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`) asks for the next due job across workspaces, so a policy scoped by one workspace GUC either refuses every claim or turns a queue into per-tenant polling. If that is wrong, the service policy should be written and this batch is the place to say so.

THEN READ WHAT THE ABSENCE OF A POLICY COSTS THE SUITE, because it is where a green run could mean least. Three outcome kinds are structurally unavailable here -- no `rows` case, no `no-effect` case (a witness needs an identity that can see the row and none exists) and no `rejected` case (RLS refuses the insert before the ledger's unique constraint is reached) -- so each table's CI negative-control entry rests on exactly TWO cases. Check that the six pinned cases are the right two per table, and that each pinned insert really is a POLICY-layer refusal: a grant-layer one would pass unchanged with row level security off and the control would report a detection it did not make.

THEN CHECK THE LEDGER'S NATURAL KEY, which is the one thing here whose absence would be silent. `unique (workspace_id, consumer, event_id)`. Without `workspace_id` the constraint is still unique, redelivery is still idempotent within one tenant, and every other check in this repository still passes -- while workspace A's consumption suppresses workspace B's redelivery and a conflicting insert becomes an oracle for another tenant's event ids. The apply-time block reads it out of pg_constraint as a sorted COLUMN SET for exactly that reason.

DISAGREE WITH THE LIFECYCLE REFUSAL IF YOU ARE GOING TO, rather than with the queue. A queue with no status column reads as a missing feature; the reason is that CTR-JOB-001's manifest reserves "lifecycle state names and transition policy" to an owner review and its envelope has no status field, so the lifecycle is the timestamps and counters the contract names. The same refusal is why the claim index is over `available_at` alone: a partial predicate naming result_ref, cancel_requested_at and the attempt budget WOULD BE that vocabulary, written where nobody reads for decisions.

AND CHECK THE CITATION CORRECTION. This batch was dispatched with "§12.6 assertion 9" for the retry-idempotence rule. §12.6 has EIGHT assertions; the sentence is §11.1 item 9. The principle is applied and the position is corrected in the migration header, in the static suite and in the open blockers -- and SMOKE_COVERAGE gains no ninth key, which is the thing to verify.
